correctness.rationale: Primitive idempotents of \(M_n(\mathbb F_q)\) are rank-one projections and hence correspond bijectively to antiflags \((P,H)\). In a full matrix ring \(eRf\ne0\) for nonzero idempotents, so the source adjacency reduces to \(ef=fe=0\), equivalent to cross-incidence. Projective counting gives \(q^{n-1}[n]_q\) vertices and degree \(q^{n-2}[n-1]_q\). For an adjacent pair, points in the two hyperplanes' intersection number \([n-2]_q\), and for each such point exactly \(q^{n-3}\) hyperplanes through the two image points avoid it, proving the constant common-neighbor count. The edge, triangle, and local-regularity statements then follow by exact double counting. The packaged checker verifies five finite instances.

value.rationale: The result upgrades the known matrix-ring connectivity picture to exact local enumerative structure across every finite field and every \(n\ge3\). Edge-regularity gives closed edge and triangle counts immediately, and in dimension three forces a locally perfect-matching graph with unique triangles through edges. The antiflag translation is a structural bridge between rank-one ring idempotents and finite projective geometry, making the result reusable rather than a one-off computation.
